content.user_title: Coordinate Metix People, Company, and Job Searches
content.value_statement: Cross-dataset research requires linked records, valid filters, and careful credit planning. This skill guides Metix API workflows using live contracts, identifier chaining, and batched retrieval.
actual_capabilities: Guide people, company, and job workflows using live API contract fields and supported query operators.
Link job employers and profile experience to company details through company identifiers.
Explain search-to-detail workflows and batch detail retrieval for up to 100 identifiers.
Distinguish structured Query Spec searches from plain-language people search.
Guide API error handling through error codes and linked Markdown documentation.
Explain contact probing, paid unlocking, batch limits, authorization scope, and worst-case credit reservations.
limitations: Provides instructions and examples, not a bundled executable client or dataset.
Authenticated operations require METIX_KEY and network access; paid contact unlocking has additional account and permission requirements.
Current field names, limits, and prices depend on the live contract and documentation.
The API retrieves records but does not provide a person-to-role scoring or ranking endpoint.

use_cases.title: Research employers before sourcing candidates
use_cases.description: Connect relevant job postings to employer records, then retrieve people at those companies without requesting contact details.

use_cases.title: Enrich a focused prospect shortlist
use_cases.description: Resolve company and people records, probe contact availability, and estimate worst-case charges before an authorized contact unlock.

use_cases.title: Plan efficient cross-dataset retrieval
use_cases.description: Check contract compatibility and credit balance, select valid filters, and batch detail requests for a large research run.

prompt_templates.title: Understand the available datasets
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how Metix people, company, and job data connect. Outline the required access and free checks. Do not run paid requests.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve a job employer
prompt_templates.prompt: For Metix job identifier [job_id], check the live contract, retrieve its title and company identifier, then retrieve that company. Exclude contact retrieval.

prompt_templates.title: Build a cross-dataset research plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a search for senior engineers at companies hiring for [role] in [location]. Use live contract fields and narrow before profile details. Estimate credits before paid calls.

prompt_templates.title: Design a controlled enrichment run
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Metix enrichment run for [shortlist] within [credit_budget]. Check key status, contract limits, batching, and contact availability. Quote worst-case unlock reservations. Wait for approval before unlocking.

output_examples.input: How should I find engineers at employers hiring for machine learning platform roles?
output: Check the live contract for supported job and people filters.
Query matching jobs, then request job details including company identifiers.
Resolve company records and narrow the employer list.
Query people at those employers and retrieve shortlisted profiles in batches.
Keep contact retrieval separate and estimate credits before paid requests.

output_examples.input: Can I unlock contact details for 40 shortlisted people?
output: Probe supports up to 50 people per request; unlock supports up to 25.
Unlock requires a paid account condition and the contact:unlock scope when using MCP.
Use current rates to quote the worst-case reservation before proceeding.
After approval, split 40 people across at least two unlock requests.

output_examples.input: METIX_KEY is missing. Can you find another key on this machine?
output_examples.output: Stop and ask the user to set METIX_KEY. Do not search the machine for another key or expose credentials.

best_practices: Read the live contract before building filters, and link datasets using returned identifiers rather than names.
Narrow searches before detail retrieval, batch identifiers, and check remaining credits before large runs.
Keep METIX_KEY out of output and files; confirm contact access authorization and worst-case charges before unlocking.
anti_patterns: Guessing field names, using unsupported operators, or sending structured filters to plain-language people search.
Retrieving one identifier per request or unlocking contacts before narrowing the shortlist and checking costs.
Searching the machine for substitute credentials or requesting a nonexistent person-to-role scoring endpoint.

faq.question: What does this skill coordinate?
faq.answer: It guides workflows that combine Metix people, company, and job data through linked identifiers.

faq.question: What access do I need?
faq.answer: Authenticated operations use METIX_KEY from the environment. Contact unlocking also requires paid account eligibility and the contact:unlock scope for MCP.

faq.question: Does this skill include a client or data?
faq.answer: No. It contains instructions and request examples. Execution requires compatible tools, network access, and the Metix service.

faq.question: Where do current filters and prices come from?
faq.answer: Use the live contract for fields and operators. Use current Metix documentation for credit formulas rather than assuming fixed prices.

faq.question: How do contact probe and unlock differ?
faq.answer: Probe checks availability for up to 50 people. Unlock returns contact values for up to 25 people and reserves worst-case charges.

faq.question: Can the API rank candidates against a role?
faq.answer: No scoring or ranking endpoint is documented here. Retrieve records and keep any subsequent reasoning separate from API capabilities.
